title: RWB-P7-E2002-APP: the values of the version answer, the entry payload, the artifact reference, the service login, the page size and the model-refusal message are fixed by no source in the read set
source: _work/msr/context/P7.md (service row, ownership rows, naming rules); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md (T3.1 defines decision_log_entry and approval only, T-A lists eight endpoints, none of them a rule-model or version answer); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P7 Decision center and log v3.md (A2.1 to A2.8); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 002 ACE plan status on the case v2.md (sections 12 to 14); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R4, R9)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 AC1, AC2, AC5; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.3; 12.4; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: Several values this slice needs are given by no source in the read set and are written as placeholders rather than guessed. (a) No source fixes the fields of the registry version answer beyond the version label and the version state: TSD P7 T-A has no such endpoint and the FSD P7 gives no shape. (b) No source fixes the field names of a decision-log item beyond rule, version, final call and decided time. (c) No source names the artifact column served with the checksum, or whether the checksum is the SHA-256 of the workbook or of the generated DRL. (d) The per-service login of DP-02 is a pattern and not a value, so the login of this service is not written out. (e) The page size of the decision-log read is given by no source; 50 is carried as a technical default only. (f) A version that is not in force, and an artifact whose checksum does not recompute, have no message identifier: the monolith had no such refusal and the model path did not exist.
evidence: Context pack P7 lists 19 provided operations and no rule-model or version-answer path, and the tables rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case with no fields; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives the 23 columns of decision_log_entry and the 22 of approval only, T3.2 gives no list for a version state, and appendix T-A lists API-P7-001 to 008 with no model or version read; FSD P7 A2.1 to A2.8 name the state of a version and the checksum check with no wire shape; the legacy story names PlanStatus, RuleResult and RuleRow as monolith Java shapes and no message for a refused version.
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-decision with the solution architect and the API owner
proposed: Publish the registry version answer and the decision-log item in the rwb-decision contract with their field names, the artifact column and the checksum it covers, the page size of the read, the login of the service and one message identifier for the two refusals, before the wave-2 contract baseline is tagged; until then the story and its fakes carry the shapes of ASM-B2-P7-018-1 to ASM-B2-P7-018-3.

title: RWB-P7-E2002-APP: the DP table adds six platform H rows, two C rows and one PLT object set that the metadata rows of the plan do not carry
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.4, R5.5 DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-15, DP-19 and R5.7 rules 1 to 8); _work/msr/wp/B2-P7-018.md (story line: H [], C [RWB-P2-E2002-CON], patterns DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19); _work/msr/context/P7.md (naming and shared platform rules)
section: Metadata (Depends on (build); Contract dependencies); 3 Preconditions; 6 INVEST check; 12.4; 12.7; 13 Pattern application
description: The patterns of this story add dependencies the metadata rows do not name: H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON (DP-04), H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON (DP-06), H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-07), H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-09), H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10), H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (DP-15) and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19), plus the outbox and inbox objects. The metadata row of the plan says Depends on (build) = None and one contract dependency, so the H rows and two C rows cannot be read from it. DP-04's C row points at RWB-P7-E1073-CON, a contract story of this service that the plan does not carry as a slice of this key, so on this APP line it is a self-reference rather than a consumed contract.
evidence: WP B2-P7-018 story line gives H [] and C [RWB-P2-E2002-CON]; Template and Rules R5.5 names the H and C rows of DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19; R5.7 rule 3 allows an H row only to the same service or a platform contract story, and rule 8 makes a story Day 1 only when it has no H outside that set; the context pack states one schema, one login, one topic, one queue and one base per service with the outbox and inbox as platform objects.
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform library owner and the rwb-decision service owner
proposed: Either complete the metadata rows from the DP table and say in R5.5 that a platform H and a self-referential C are held by the platform and contract stories and are not repeated on the APP line, or keep the plan rows as they are and read the DP rows as dependencies added by the patterns, as section 13 of this story does.

title: RWB-P7-E2002-APP: the width of one ledger entry is ambiguous where a move runs two rules in one transaction, and no source fixes the payload that carries the plan facts
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P7 Decision center and log v3.md (A2.2 and A2.3, AC-P7-002-01, AC-ALT-P7-001-02); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2.md (T3.1 decision_log_entry, T3.3 relationships); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 002 ACE plan status on the case v2.md (sections 4, 7, 9 and 11)
section: 7 AC3, AC4; 8 BR2, BR3; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.4
description: The legacy story moves the route state twice in one transaction, from PLAN_CURE_PERIOD to PLAN_BROKEN by R-RES-29 and then to BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION by R-RES-30, and writes a decision log entry for each move. The ledger holds one entry per decision and the record carries one rule and one version, so it is ambiguous whether the two moves are two entries or one entry naming the rule of the final call with the second rule and the intermediate state in its actions. No source fixes the payload that carries the plan reference, the plan status and its date: TSD P7 T3.1 gives inputs_ref and two jsonb columns and no content model, and the legacy story carries the values in Java facts.
evidence: FSD P7 A2.2 and A2.3 describe one entry per event with a rule ID, a rule version and an inputs reference; TSD P7 T3.1 has one rule_id, one rule_version, inputs_ref varchar(400), actions jsonb and outcome jsonb with no content model; the legacy story section 4 step 7 says an entry is written for each move, section 9 moves the state twice, and section 11 gives the rule_row fields read by rule ID and package version.
owner_role: Service owner of rwb-decision with the rwb-case service owner and the data owner
proposed: State in the decision-record contract that one entry is written per case, business date and rule identity, and that a transaction running two rules writes one entry per rule; publish the content model of the inputs snapshot and of the actions payload, with the plan reference, the plan status and its date inside them.

title: RWB-P7-E2002-APP: the legacy story sits in Module P2 Integration and names the plan-status endpoint on the monolith base, while the plan gives this APP slice to rwb-decision and the read to rwb-integration
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 002 ACE plan status on the case v2.md (metadata Module P2 Integration; sections 12, 13 and 19); _work/msr/wp/B2-P7-018.md (story line: service rwb-decision, contract RWB-P2-E2002-CON, file under RWB-SVC-P7); _work/msr/context/P7.md (rwb-decision owns the rule registry, the decision log and the approvals)
section: Metadata (Service); 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 12.1; 12.2; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy key is filed under P2 Integration and its own endpoint GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/plan-status is a P2 operation that reads ACE and stores the plan status through P3. The realignment puts the APP slice of the same key in rwb-decision, whose ownership rows are the rule registry, the decision log and the approvals and which owns no plan-status path. The two readings cannot both be served from one service: the plan read is rwb-integration's under RWB-P2-E2002-CON and this story may only consume it, so the story is written as the registry and record side of the plan status and the plan-status endpoint stays out of its provided set.
evidence: Legacy story metadata Module P2 Integration, section 12 endpoint GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/plan-status with the stored plan status written through P3, section 13 a P2 package and configuration; WP B2-P7-018 places the APP story in service rwb-decision with RWB-P2-E2002-CON as its contract dependency and the file in the RWB-SVC-P7 folder; context pack P7 ownership rows list no plan-status or plan table for rwb-decision.
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-decision and rwb-integration service owners
proposed: Keep the plan read and the stored status with rwb-integration and rwb-case and confirm that the rwb-decision slice of the key is the registry version and the decision record, or move this APP story to rwb-integration if the plan read must stay with it; restate the legacy endpoint on the per-service base of the owner in either case.
